title: Secret Keepers: The Impact of LLMs on Linguistic Markers of Personal Traits

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the predictive power of classifiers and lexical dictionaries on original versus LLM-rewritten texts to measure how LLMs alter gender-specific linguistic markers, including tracking the direction of misclassifications (e.g., analyzing if LLMs skew predictions from female to male).

Evaluating shifts in age-predictive linguistic patterns by classifying original texts against LLM-rewritten texts and observing whether LLM generation systematically shifts the perceived author profile toward older age groups.

Using data-driven classifiers and top-down lexical analysis to predict political affiliation (Democrat vs. Republican) from text, and assessing how LLM involvement washes away political markers or skews predictions in a specific partisan direction.

Employing bottom-up machine learning classifiers and top-down dictionary methods (e.g., LIWC, MFD2) to measure how LLM rewriting alters linguistic markers associated with personality (Big Five), dispositional empathy, and moral foundations.
